From 35d0ed82d03e5ee77ea4f31f20e29562a7721649 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Raphael Zimmer <raphael.zimmer@tu-ilmenau.de>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:08:12 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] libceph: Fix potential out-of-bounds access in
 osdmap_decode()

When decoding osd_state and osd_weight from an incoming osdmap in
osdmap_decode(), both are decoded for each osd, i.e., map->max_osd
times. The ceph_decode_need() check only accounts for
sizeof(*map->osd_weight) once. This can potentially result in an
out-of-bounds memory access if the incoming message is corrupted such
that the max_osd value exceeds the actual content of the osdmap message.

This patch fixes the issue by changing the corresponding part in the
ceph_decode_need() check to account for
map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight).

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: dcbc919a5dc8 ("libceph: switch osdmap decoding to use ceph_decode_entity_addr")
Signed-off-by: Raphael Zimmer <raphael.zimmer@tu-ilmenau.de>
Reviewed-by: Ilya Dryomov <idryomov@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ilya Dryomov <idryomov@gmail.com>

diff --git a/net/ceph/osdmap.c b/net/ceph/osdmap.c
index 669348d883f0..2095e73ccf6c 100644
--- a/net/ceph/osdmap.c
+++ b/net/ceph/osdmap.c
@@ -1705,7 +1705,7 @@ static int osdmap_decode(void **p, void *end, bool msgr2,
 	ceph_decode_need(p, end, 3*sizeof(u32) +
 			 map->max_osd*(struct_v >= 5 ? sizeof(u32) :
 						       sizeof(u8)) +
-				       sizeof(*map->osd_weight), e_inval);
+			 map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight), e_inval);
 	if (ceph_decode_32(p) != map->max_osd)
 		goto e_inval;
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a potential out-of-bounds memory access in the `osdmap_decode()` function in `net/ceph/osdmap.c`. The vulnerability occurs when decoding `osd_weight` for each OSD: the previous `ceph_decode_need()` check only reserved space for a single weight entry instead of `map->max_osd` entries, allowing a crafted or corrupted message to trigger an out-of-bounds read.

### Modifications in each file:
- **`net/ceph/osdmap.c`**: In the `osdmap_decode()` function, the `ceph_decode_need()` call that checks the remaining buffer size for decoding OSD weights was corrected. The expression `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` was replaced with `map->max_osd * sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` to properly account for the total required space across all OSDs.

### Relationships:
- The single change in `osdmap.c` addresses the root cause: a miscalculation in the buffer length validation. By multiplying the weight size by `map->max_osd`, the fix ensures that the `ceph_decode_need()` macro correctly verifies that enough data is available for all OSD weight entries, preventing an out-of-bounds access when decoding the OSD map.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
ceph_decode_need(p, end, 3*sizeof(u32) +
			 map->max_osd*(struct_v >= 5 ? sizeof(u32) :
						       sizeof(u8)) +
			 sizeof(*map->osd_weight), e_inval);
...
for (i = 0; i < map->max_osd; i++)
	map->osd_weight[i] = ceph_decode_32(p);
Reason:
The `ceph_decode_need()` check only accounted for a single `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` byte, but the subsequent loop reads `map->max_osd` entries of 4 bytes each. If the incoming message is corrupted with an artificially large `max_osd`, the insufficient size check allows memory access beyond the allocated buffer, resulting in an out‑of‑bounds read.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
ceph_decode_need(p, end, 3*sizeof(u32) +
			 map->max_osd*(struct_v >= 5 ? sizeof(u32) :
						       sizeof(u8)) +
			 map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight), e_inval);
Reason:
The fix multiplies `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` by `map->max_osd` in the size check, ensuring that enough space is verified for all expected `osd_weight` entries before the loop. This prevents the out‑of‑bounds access when decoding a corrupted osdmap.
